name: role-change-dialog
title: Role change dialog
description: Confirm a role change by showing what the person gains and loses in plain words, and ask for the email to be typed before anyone is made an owner.
docs: Pass member ({ name, email, image }), fromRole and toRole ({ id, name, capabilities, powerful }) and onConfirm. Every role lists everything it allows (a string, or { id, label }), and the dialog works out Gains and Loses from the two lists, with a count of what stays the same, so the change reads right however many roles you have. The two lists sit side by side once the panel is 28rem wide and both have something to show; a side with nothing on it is one quiet line across the full width. onConfirm({ member, fromRole, toRole }) may return a promise: the field locks, the button shows progress and the dialog will not close; on success the form becomes 'Role changed' and 'Dana Whitfield now has the Editor role.' with focus on Done when the focus was in the panel (a panel that nobody pressed by hand never takes focus or scrolls the page), and on a rejection the form stays with the Error's message above the buttons and the button says Try again. warnOnDowngrade (default true) adds a note when something is taken away. A toRole with powerful: true asks for the member's email (their name when there is none) to be typed, and the button stays off until it matches. lastOwner refuses a change that takes something away and says why; blockedReason refuses any other change in your own words; two roles that allow the same say so. It is an alert dialog, so focus starts on Cancel: trigger is the element that opens it, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it, and RoleChangePanel is the inside on its own (standalone). labels translates every word and locale the counts.
